title: What If You Always Played Your Music Too Loud?

scenes.text: What if you always played your music at full volume? The damage is silent, until it isn't.
Your ears can handle 85 decibels for eight hours. Every three decibels louder halves that time.
Earbuds at max hit about 100 decibels. That's safe for roughly fifteen minutes a day.
After a loud night, ringing in your ears is the warning: tiny hair cells in your inner ear are hurt.
You're born with about fifteen thousand of them per ear, and once they die, they never grow back.
The World Health Organization says 1.1 billion young people are at risk. Turning it down is the only fix.
